title: Reduce-scatter, all-gather, and communication volume
goal:
Section 7 says that an all-reduce is a reduce-scatter followed by an all-gather, and that each moves $\Psi$ elements per process. Simulate that in NumPy. Each worker's data is one row of a 2D array, so `xs[i]` is worker `i`'s vector.

Write three functions and one table:

- `reduce_scatter(xs)` sums `xs` over workers and returns a list of `nd` shards. Worker `i` keeps shard `i`, which is chunk `i` of the sum. Split with `np.array_split` so that lengths needn't divide evenly.
- `all_gather(shards)` returns a list of `nd` arrays. Each is the concatenation of all shards.
- `all_reduce(xs)` is `all_gather(reduce_scatter(xs))`.
- `comm_volume(stage)` returns the elements moved per process per step, in units of $\Psi$ (Section 7.1 and Section 7.2). Use 0 for plain data parallelism, and 1, 2, 3 for the ZeRO stages.
hints: A reduce-scatter reduces first and scatters second. Sum over axis 0, then cut the result into `nd` chunks.
Data parallelism does one all-reduce on gradients: $2\Psi$. Stages 1 and 2 swap it for a reduce-scatter of gradients plus an all-gather of updated parameters.
Stage 3 gathers parameters twice, once in the forward pass and once in the backward pass (Section 7.2.2), on top of the reduce-scatter of gradients.
